metas.name: Black on Yellow Chevron
metas.note: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir. (The yellow is somewhat orange-ish)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Bodrum Architecture
metas.note: Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue (or light pink) details or unpainted stone walls.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Bursa Green Signs and Infrastructure
metas.note:
Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

  • NOTE: Several other types of infrastructure in Bursa, such as fences and guardrails, may also be coloured green.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Cotton Fields in Turkey
metas.note: Cotton is mainly found in the region surrounding the city of Şanlıurfa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Eastern Divider
metas.note:
Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.

  • Beware that divided highways with clear dividers, such as guardrails, can still be found in the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Flat Roofs
metas.note: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Goreme
metas.note: Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Horizontal Tanks with Vertical Tanks Under
metas.note: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to Elâzığ.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Istanbul Street Signs
metas.note:
Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

  • Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Izmir Province Street Signs
metas.note: Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Lake Van
metas.note: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Metal Roofs
metas.note:
Metal roofs are most common in the east.

  • Note that for this and the other roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Mount Ararat
metas.note: Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Nevşehir Province Buildings
metas.note: Many buildings in the Nevşehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Northeast Hills
metas.note:
In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

Some of the new Gen 4 truck coverage is greener since it was also taken in the spring.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Olive Trees
metas.note: Olive trees are mainly found on the Mediterranean coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Phone Codes in Turkey
metas.note: Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Pyramid Metal Roofs
metas.note: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: River Cliff Valleys
metas.note: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Road with Extreme Fog
metas.note: This Road with extreme fog and yellow lines can be seen southeast of Izmit.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Spherical Water Tanks
metas.note: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Square Water Tanks
metas.note: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from İskenderun to Sanliurfa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Street Signs in Ankara Province
metas.note:
Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.

Beware that some newer street signs are red.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Sunflowers
metas.note: Sunflowers are mainly found in northwestern Turkey.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Tea Plantations
metas.note: Tea plantations are common in the province of Rize
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Tiled Roofs
metas.note:
Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.

  • Note that for this and the other roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkish Greenhouses
metas.note: If you find yourself surrounded by greenhouses, you are likely to be along the south coast west of Adana.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkish Pines
metas.note:
Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

  • NOTE: Turkish pines can appear very similar to Aleppo pines, which are uncommon in Turkey, but are often found in other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkish Vineyards
metas.note: A majority of all vineyards in Turkey can be found in a region east of Izmir.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Volcanic Rocks
metas.note: Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Yellow on Black Chevron
metas.note: Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the Balıkesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.
